newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open softer as metals sag.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open softer as metals sag.

text.p: The Australian share market softened at the open on Wednesday after base metal prices sagged in offshore markets.
The All Ordinaries index lost 3.8 points to 2,497.0.
Big miners, BHP, down 22 cents to A$17.64 (US$13.67), and WMC, down seven cents to A$8.23, suffered most early after copper and nickel prices slid.
Industrial leaders News Corp, down five cents at A$7.04, and National Australia Bank, six cents lower at A$16.63, saw profit-taking after Tuesday's rally.
"The market is not stepping up at the moment," said equities adviser Dirk Van Der Struyf of brokerage Hartley Poynton.
"It is still probably a tad nervous on some of the base metals even though most of them are showing signs of slow recovery."

Featuring early was Perth casino owner-operator Burswood Property Trust which had 39.7 million units traded, the bulk of it in a number of lines crossed through BZW Australia. Speculation centred on a Japanese investor selling out of their stake and brokers said the units appeared to have gone to a range of institutional investors.
Results continued apace with insurance group GIO Australia adding three cents to A$3.74 after reporting a 22 percent higher half year net profit of A$102.5 million.
Petroleum retail holding company Caltex Australia added three cents to A$4.30 after a 36 percent higher year net profit of A$57.7 million.
Rises slightly shaded falls, while 45 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
